description: Deerns used IESVE to calibrate an energy model for a coastal hotel described as being on a mountain above Monaco. Inputs included as-built records, site visits, utility bills, meters and building-management-system records. The model was calibrated against consumption from May 2022 to April 2023. It was then used to compare HVAC, shading and operational measures for a 2030 energy-reduction roadmap. The hotel name is not given. The listing says Monaco while the narrative refers to French regulation; no country identity or achieved 2030 compliance is inferred. This public HTML case narrative is published by IES and can be read without payment. Its reuse licence is not stated. Access to the described software, input data and project models is not established by the public page. The source does not give a complete study period or all spatial and temporal model resolutions. Reported results are provider claims and have not been independently reproduced. The case supports the documented infrastructure simulation use and is linked to the named modelling resources. Only metadata and the case description were inspected; no data or model files were downloaded.
